mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.2% (current value 0.16%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation and encourages risk-taking, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active as FEDFUNDS is continuously observable.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS <= 0.2% in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 228.5 (current value 228.527) indicates accelerating inflation, which typically precedes monetary tightening and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to market anticipation of rate cuts.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 228.5 in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is at or below 0.2% (FEDFUNDS <= 0.2) and unemployment is at or above 8.0% (UNRATE >= 8.0), the economy is in a monetary easing cycle with high unemployment, which typically produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to accommodative policy and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: The condition (FEDFUNDS<=0.2 AND UNRATE>=8.0) is met in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 230), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns as investors anticipate aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation, reducing risk appetite and equity valuations.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 230 in 60% of instances but 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST > 700) indicate strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are supported by robust consumer spending.
failure_condition: HOUST > 700 in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100 (current value 97.2853), it signals strong economic activity and robust corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth is strong (PAYEMS > 133000) and unemployment is falling (UNRATE < 8.0), the labor market signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: The condition (PAYEMS>133000 AND UNRATE<8.0) is met in 60% of instances but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0, current value 8.2) signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors flee risk.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.0 in 60% of instances but 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those cases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
